title: Edible Gel Electrophoresis
author: Hannah Zurcher
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.t3neqme

steps.title: Prepare gelatin solution
steps.instruction: In a heat‑safe bowl, add the amount of hot water specified on the gelatin packet (approximately half of the total water required for the brand) to the gelatin powder and stir until fully dissolved.

steps.title: Cast gel to correct depth
steps.instruction: Pour the dissolved gelatin into a takeaway container, filling it to a depth of 1.5 cm (0.5 in).

steps.title: Set gel in refrigerator
steps.instruction: Place the container in a refrigerator and allow the gelatin to set completely.

steps.title: Remove solidified gel
steps.instruction: Take the container out of the refrigerator; the gel should be firm.

steps.title: Create wells in gel
steps.instruction: Using a butter knife, gently press the tip into one end of the gel to form wells that extend approximately halfway into the agar.

steps.title: Add colored dye to wells
steps.instruction: Place one or two drops of food dye into each well, using a different color for each well.

steps.title: Prepare foil electrodes
steps.instruction: Cut two strips of foil to be as long as the width of the gel roll and about 1 inch wide; fold each strip flat to make a thin strip.

steps.title: Attach foil strips to batteries
steps.instruction: Tape one foil strip to the positive terminal of a battery and the other strip to the negative terminal of a second battery.

steps.title: Position electrodes on gel
steps.instruction: Lay the taped foil strips at opposite ends of the gel container, placing the negative‑end strip near the wells and the positive‑end strip at the opposite side.

steps.title: Add running buffer
steps.instruction: Pour a carbonated beverage (used as buffer) into the container until the liquid level is 1 cm above the surface of the gel.

steps.title: Run electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Connect the batteries to allow current to flow; let the gel run for about 10 minutes, watching the dye migrate, and stop before the front overruns the gel.

steps.title: Recover and view gel
steps.instruction: Carefully remove the gel from the container and place it on white paper or fondant to observe the separated colors.

steps.title: Document results
steps.instruction: Clean the workspace, then post photos of the finished gel to Instagram (@eleutherophobia.h, @mingy2310) or Twitter (@h_zurcher, @realMingChia).
